coaching.headline: A dominant Kira and a won jungle lane covered three unfavored lanes for a ranked win, closed out by a five-for-one teamfight at their Inner Tower.
coaching.team: Draft read two lanes favored, carry against Eden and jungle against Wukong, against three unfavored: midlane against Gideon, offlane against Morigesh, and support against Aurora, each reading unfavored or "theirs" the whole game. Kira opened with first blood on Eden at 7.3 and never lost the carry lane from there, while Scarlett held the jungle matchup against Wukong throughout. The first crack came at 10.4: Iggy & Scorch and Phase lost a two-for-zero skirmish alone in the enemy jungle with no objective up, while Kira and Scarlett both stood ahead and untouched in their own lanes — a rotate from either would have evened the numbers. At 14.3 we lost another fight 0-2, this time at our own Fangtooth, but the camp still went to us in the same window, a trade rather than a clean loss. From there the team won three more fights outright — 22.5, 24.3, and 30.5 — on top of the 12m skirmish won earlier; only one of the four won fights all game, the 24.3 fight that turned straight into Fangtooth a minute later, got cashed into a prize within 90 seconds, while the 22.5 double kill at their Outer Tower and the 30.5 teamfight both went unconverted into a structure in the moment, even though towers finished even at five apiece. Vision favored the team most of the game too, 50 wards placed to their 44, with three of theirs destroyed against one of ours. Greystone's death caught alone by Wukong at minute 29 cost Orb Prime and then the Inner Tower soon after, but the team answered immediately with a five-for-one teamfight at their Inner Tower that broke the game open and closed it out.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The moment that decided the game was the response to that rough patch at the end: down Orb Prime and a body after Greystone was caught alone by Wukong at minute 29, the team grouped instead of scattering and won a five-for-one at their Inner Tower, with Kira alone taking four of the five kills. That fight broke the tower line open and closed the game out shortly after.
coaching.whatWorked: The clearest strength was Kira, who finished 12 kills against a single death and the team's highest hero damage at 39,153 — the same player who opened the game with first blood on Eden at 7.3 and closed it with four kills alone in the final teamfight.

His only death came at 10.5, in the two-for-zero skirmish at 10.4 in the enemy jungle — a fight that went bad while Kira and Scarlett both stood ahead and untouched in their own lanes, and a rotate from either would have flipped the numbers.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Kira won the carry lane against Eden outright, opening with first blood at 7.3 and finishing 12 kills against one death, the team's highest hero damage at 39,153. Her only death, at 14.3, came in the fight at the team's own Fangtooth and directly preceded them taking the Outer Tower soon after; everything else was Kira finding kills solo, including four alone in the 30.5 teamfight that closed the game.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Scarlett won the jungle matchup against Wukong throughout but was caught and killed alone three times before minute 21, one of them at 20.7 directly preceding them taking a tower soon after. All four items in her build pushed physical power with no magical armor anywhere in it, against a comp that ran three magical damage threats to two physical — the exact gap the matchup data flagged.
perPlayer.ec0e3ed7-0f49-4ffe-8aa0-c49af17ea4fe: Greystone lost the offlane matchup to Morigesh all game but still finished 4 kills, 1 death, and 2 assists, taking a team-high 61,952 damage and mitigating 68,618 of it while picking off Eden twice plus one each on Gideon and Aurora. His only death, caught alone by Wukong at minute 29, directly preceded them taking both Orb Prime and the Inner Tower — the single costliest death of the game.
perPlayer.3bacbb54-d965-4b48-9a67-f176f7d04cd5: Iggy & Scorch never got the mid lane going against Gideon, reading "theirs all game" from the first check, and finished with four deaths, second-most on the team behind Scarlett's five, including being caught alone twice, once by the enemy carry and once by the enemy offlane. His one kill came in the 24.3 fight that turned straight into Fangtooth a minute later, the shape of play that worked all night: grouped, on top of the objective.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: Zero kills but 21,652 healing and 14 assists kept Phase useful out of a lane that read unfavored the whole game; the one death came in an early skirmish neither Kira nor Scarlett rotated to help.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.text: Kira: 12 kills, 1 death, and a team-high 39,153 hero damage — first blood at 7.3 through four kills alone in the 30.5 teamfight, as clean a carry line as it gets.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.text: Scarlett: 0 kills and 5 deaths despite winning the jungle lane outright; three of those deaths were solo picks, and the build carried no magical armor into a three-magical enemy comp.

ec0e3ed7-0f49-4ffe-8aa0-c49af17ea4fe.text: Greystone: 4 kills and 1 death is a strong line out of a losing offlane matchup, but that single death at minute 29 handed over Orb Prime and the Inner Tower in the same stretch.

3bacbb54-d965-4b48-9a67-f176f7d04cd5.text: Pinned in a losing mid lane all game, Iggy & Scorch finished with four deaths, second-most on the team behind Scarlett's five, and only one kill — landed in the fight that actually converted into Fangtooth.

22.5.call: Kira isolated Eden and Aurora alone near their Outer Tower and killed both for a clean two-for-zero, even with two items on the field to their four. Nothing fell afterward, though — the kills never turned into the tower itself. The lesson from an otherwise perfect read: follow a pick like that with the group so it becomes a structure, not just a reset.

24.3.call: Iggy & Scorch and Kira grouped for a clean three-for-zero at the team's own Fangtooth, and this one turned straight into the camp, secured a minute later at 25. That's the only one of four won fights that actually got cashed into an objective — the shape every other win needed to copy.

30.5.call: The biggest fight of the game came right after conceding Orb Prime and losing Greystone caught alone at minute 29. Instead of scattering, the team grouped for a five-for-one at their Inner Tower, with Kira alone taking four of the five kills, even while well behind on items in that fight, 12 to their 19. Regrouping instead of chasing the lost objective is what turned the game.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase's build followed Marshal and Enra's Blessing into the winning core, then diverted to Windcaller instead of Galaxy Greaves for the third slot — trading the 30/30 dual armor, ability haste, and mana regen Galaxy Greaves offers for more magical power and healing amplification instead. That left defensive stats light until Vanguardian finally added armor and tenacity in the fourth slot. Against a comp that ran three magical damage threats to two physical, with Eden alone doing 30,792 damage to enemy heroes, earlier armor would have been the more useful layer for a support standing in every fight. Phase still closed with 21,652 healing and 14 assists, so the sustain the build did prioritize was not wasted.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vesh adds a damage-over-time tick to every ability hit on a hero, which fits a link-and-buff support whose own kit and allies are landing frequent poke rather than one big burst. It offers no defensive stat of its own, so it leans on the frontline to hold aggro — which matched this game, since Greystone carried the team's highest damage taken and mitigated.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Kira skipped the winning core of Solaris, Ashbringer, and Imperator entirely and built an execute-and-anti-heal kit instead: Vanquisher's execute damage, Tainted Rounds' healing cut that ramps as the target drops low, and Scattershot and Onixian Quiver's extra homing projectiles for faster clears and burst. The winning core leans on Solaris' on-hit self-heal and Ashbringer's cooldown refunds for sustained trading; what Kira built instead is built to finish low targets and answer sustain rather than duel evenly. With a healer on the enemy side, Tainted Rounds' healing cut was a direct answer to that threat. The output backed it up — 39,153 hero damage, 12 kills, and a single death.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Demiurge boosts the stats every item grants and the damage every item effect deals, which compounds on a six-item board this heavy on on-hit procs like Vanquisher's execute and Tainted Rounds' anti-heal. It adds no durability of its own, but that trade would have cost little here since Kira died only once all game with Phase and Greystone absorbing damage around her.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Scarlett's four completed items, Manta Scythe, Malady, Earthshaker, and Infernum, are all pure physical power, penetration, and haste with zero defensive stats between them; there's no meta core logged for her on this hero to compare against, but the matchup flag is explicit: no magic resist against a comp that ran three magical damage threats to two physical. The build is aimed at clearing camps and bursting fights fast — Manta Scythe's bonus monster damage and Malady's execute-style burst both point that way, not at surviving being dived. That's consistent with the game she had: modest hero damage at 4,574 against 36,348 damage taken and five deaths, despite winning the jungle lane outright.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Krix's flat and per-level bonus to maximum health is a pure survivability minor, exactly what a full-offense item board like this one was missing. It adds no damage of its own, so the trade is giving up some of the burst the item build was chasing for more time alive in a fight — worth it here given how often Scarlett was caught and killed alone.

ec0e3ed7-0f49-4ffe-8aa0-c49af17ea4fe.build: Greystone completed the full winning core, Overlord, Rapture, and Aegis Of Agawar, then added Catalytic Drive and Cursed Scroll as two extra off-meta slots rather than more pure resistance. Aegis' scaling armor, which doubles under 40% health, and Overlord's stacking cleave already cover a lot of frontline duty; Catalytic Drive's execute-and-heal and Cursed Scroll's self-damage-for-attack-speed trade lean the extra slots toward finishing fights rather than surviving longer. That's a reasonable bet for a hero already absorbing the most damage on the team, 61,952 taken and 68,618 mitigated, and it held up: 4 kills, 1 death, with the one death a solo catch at minute 29.
ec0e3ed7-0f49-4ffe-8aa0-c49af17ea4fe.eternal: Krix's health-scaling bonus fits a frontline bruiser whose job is soaking damage for the rest of the team, which lines up directly with Greystone's team-high 61,952 damage taken this game. The trade is no offensive scaling from the eternal slot, leaning entirely on the item board, which already skewed toward finishing power with Catalytic Drive and Cursed Scroll, for damage instead.

3bacbb54-d965-4b48-9a67-f176f7d04cd5.build: Iggy & Scorch matched two of the three winning-core items, Orb Of Enlightenment (the evolved form of Orb Of Growth) and Megacosm, but skipped Entropy for Tainted Scepter, World Breaker, and Caustica instead. Entropy adds flat bonus damage to every ability hit; what he built instead leans on Tainted Scepter's healing cut against the enemy's healer and Caustica's armor penetration against their frontline, a defensible read on this matchup, but neither adds the survivability Entropy's raw damage add-on would have traded for. The gap showed up in the lane more than the build: "theirs all game" against Gideon and four deaths, second-most on the team behind Scarlett's five, with only one kill to show for it.
3bacbb54-d965-4b48-9a67-f176f7d04cd5.eternal: Demiurge amplifies item stats and item-effect damage, which suits a kit built around stacking item procs like Tainted Scepter's Malice stacks and Caustica's armor shred. It adds nothing defensive, and for a midlaner losing the lane matchup all game and dying four times, that's a real trade-off — the item board, not the eternal slot, was the bigger gap to close first.

threats: Heal-stacking: Aurora. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
ourKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
ourKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
ourKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Oil Spill → Molotov ignite → Flame Turret → Inferno knockback ult
ourKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

enemyKits.combo: stance-swap with Zero Shift → Tachyon Lance (ranged) or melee chain → Limit Break on Overheat
enemyKits.winCondition: build Heat and burst with Limit Break, flexing range and melee
enemyKits.passive: damage builds Heat → Overheat unlocks Limit Break
enemyKits.playWith: peel that lets her ramp Heat safely
enemyKits.playAgainst: pressure her before Overheat; CC during the melee stance

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
enemyKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
enemyKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

enemyKits.combo: Mark a target → Hive slow → Swarm reposition → Curse execute-burst ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Mark + Curse a squishy and delete them with %max-HP Pestilence
enemyKits.playWith: setup that holds her marked target
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's squishy with one escape (Swarm) — dive after it's used; spread vs Hive

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain
